Newcastle chief: Summer was 'not chaotic' with Howe exit prepared for
highlights.summary: Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson says they were "prepared for a number of months" for Eddie Howe's exit in a summer that "never felt chaotic".
body: Howe's shock resignation in July led to the swift appointment of Matthias Jaissle, who has enjoyed an unbeaten start to his reign.
Howe's exit was part of a turbulent summer for the Magpies which also included the departures of key players Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.
Toon chief Wilson revealed Howe's resignation was not "painful" because of their Jaissle contingency, but Guimaraes' £75m move to Arsenal was not "part of the plan".
Wilson said: "Eddie is an exceptionally talented coach and at some point that meant he was probably going to do something else and we had to be prepared for that.

highlights.title: Forza Horizon 6 has not been delayed on PS5, developer confirms - but still won't say when it's coming out
highlights.summary: Forza Horizon 6 developer Playground Games has shot down rumours the game's anticipated PlayStation 5 version had been delayed. The confirmation, slim as it is, comes a little over one week after reports about a quiet delay for Horizon 6 started surfacing.
body: In a blog post covering Forza Horizon 6's latest major update, Playground reaffirmed the open-world driving game is coming to PS5 this year, though without announcing a solid release date or suggesting a release window.

"If you're planning your trip to Discover Japan on PlayStation 5, stay tuned! Forza Horizon 6 will be releasing on PS5 later this year, and you can add the game to your wishlist on the PlayStation Store to be notified of availability," reads a paragraph tucked away near the end of the post.

This was certainly surprising to see, as even before last week's reports, players just assumed the game had quietly slipped out of 2026 simply because the developer stopped talking about it. Horizon 6 was revealed during 2025's Tokyo Game Show, almost exactly one year ago. It made sense, given the game's Japan setting, so it would likewise make sense for Xbox to return to the TGS stage to announce a PS5 release date. TGS 2026 takes place 17th-21st September, so we won't have to wait too long to get our answer.

highlights.title: ‘So big and so close’: going on a bear hunt in northern Spain
highlights.summary: Conservationists have helped Cantabrian brown bears claw their way back from the edge of extinction in the beautiful mountains of Asturias – and carefully controlled nature tourism allows visitors to see them.
body: Once upon a time, in the woods outside Pola de Somiedo, lived a family of Cantabrian brown bears. The villagers reported sightings of a mother bear who had lost a leg to a hunter’s trap, her two cubs and two adult males, either of which might have been the father. In those days, at the end of the 1980s, they seemed to be the last of their kind in this part of Asturias. Meanwhile, the wider population dropped to about 60 bears across the surrounding Cantabrian mountain range that gave the species its name.

They have since clawed their way back from the edge of extinction here in northern Spain, and nature guide Luis Frechilla believes their numbers may now be upwards of 500 again. “They’re still classed as endangered,” he tells me, until the official count hits 1,000. But relative abundance makes them much easier to see today in Somiedo natural park – one of Spain’s first such protected areas, established in 1988.

highlights.title: Xiaomi’s wide foldable promises more power than Samsung’s
highlights.summary: Xiaomi is the latest manufacturer to release a short, wide foldable phone, in the week Apple is expected to do the same. I got to try the 18 Fold behind closed doors at IFA last week, and while it looks and feels similar enough to Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8, superior specs make it feel like the…
body: A triple camera, big battery, and new Arm GPU make the 18 Fold a phone to be reckoned with.

The 18 Fold is Xiaomi’s first book-style foldable since 2024’s Mix Fold 4, but the company has followed Huawei and Samsung in moving to a short, squat design. Xiaomi’s phone goes further though: it’s both shorter and wider than Samsung’s, with a roughly 1.4:1 aspect ratio on both the 7.58-inch inner and 5.38-inch outer screens — almost an exact match for both international paper sizes and IMAX screens, meaning this may be the one phone capable of playing The Odyssey without letterboxing.

In practice, this still feels similar to the Z Fold 8 though. It’s compact and pocketable when closed and the cover screen is comfortable to use single-handed — though I expect it too will have issues with some apps running awkwardly on the short screen. When open this is a natural form factor for watching movies or reading ebooks, if perhaps slightly less well suited to multitasking work, though Xiaomi still includes both split-screen apps and floating windows with multitasking in mind.

highlights.title: Opaque recurrence, and other AI terms that you should probably know
highlights.summary: The rise of AI has brought an avalanche of new terms and slang. Here is a glossary with definitions of some of the most important words and phrases you might encounter.
body: AI is rewriting the world and, at the same time, inventing a whole new language to describe how it’s doing it. Sit in on any product meeting, pitch, or panel these days, and you’ll hear people toss around LLMs, RAG, RLHF — and, as of last week, terms like “opaque recurrence,” the reasoning technique in OpenAI’s new Astra model that’s got AI safety researchers rattled. The vocabulary moves fast enough to make even very smart people in the tech world feel a little insecure.

This glossary is our attempt to fix that: plain-English definitions of the AI terms you’re most likely to see, whether you’re building with this stuff, investing in it, or just trying to keep up by reading TechCrunch or listening to related podcasts. We update it regularly as the field evolves, so consider it a living document, much like the AI systems it describes.

highlights.summary: As a Test summer during which English cricket appeared to be in crisis nears its end, Joe Root's side go into their final fixture against Pakistan with the only major talking point being whether the bowling attack will be rotated.
body: Barring the discovery of any more England off-field issues before the start of the third Test at Edgbaston on Wednesday, it's Pakistan making all the noise after sacking their head coach and replacing seven members of their touring squad following defeats at Headingley and Lord's.

Brydon Carse remains absent from England's 15-player group at Edgbaston after the fast bowler was briefly arrested following an incident outside a Derby nightclub in August. Fellow quick Matthew Fisher has been dropped, but the rest of the group were all part of the squad at Lord's last time out.
With a series victory sealed, England could choose to give some of their cross-format players a rest ahead of upcoming white-ball contests with Sri Lanka.
If the third Test were to go all five days, the first of three T20 internationals would start just two days later, before three 50-over matches follow later in September.

highlights.title: Tom Hiddleston's Return to Streaming Has Officially Been Confirmed
highlights.summary: Ever since being cast as Loki in the first Marvel 's Thor movie back in 2011, Tom Hiddleston has been one of the busiest actors in Hollywood. He’s dominated the big screen in both Marvel and non-Marvel movies and the same can be said for the small screen as well.
body: Hiddleston will co-star in the Apple TV film Tenzing, a biographical film about Tenzing Norgay, the Nepalese Sherpa who guided New Zealand mountaineer Sir Edmund Hillary when they became the first men to reach the top of Mount Everest. Hiddleston will play Hillary, while Chinese actor Genden Phuntsok will star as Norgay. Willem Dafoe also stars as John Hunt, the British army officer who led the expedition to Everest.

The movie was directed by Australian filmmaker Jennifer Peedom. This will be Peedom’s first narrative film, though she has extensive experience as a documentary filmmaker, particularly on the subject of mountain climbing. She has directed the documentaries Miracle on Everest (2008), Sherpa (2015), Mountain (2017), and Mountain Quest (2021). For Tenzing, Peedom filmed around Mount Everest, along with the Nepalese city of Kathmandu.

“The extraordinary thing that Jen has done is she's put us all in the environment,” Hiddleston said in a 2025 interview with Josh Horowitz. “We've actually just spent a month in Nepal and I've spent some time in the Khumbu Valley and in the foothills of Everest and in the Himalayas.”

highlights.title: Laura Poitras and Rachel Lauren Mueller on Making ICE Doc ‘They’re Here’ Like a “Horror Movie”
highlights.summary: The Oscar-winning filmmaker and Minneapolis-based journalist chronicle the Minneapolis resistance movement to ICE’s paramilitary occupation, which resulted in the fatal shootings of Renée Good and Alex Pretti.
body: That’s the message of Oscar-winning documentarian Laura Poitras, whose new short documentary They’re Here chronicles how Immigration Customs Enforcement troops invaded and occupied Minneapolis last year, and the anonymous residents who resisted.

Stylistically, the film draws from horror and sci-fi cinema to depict how a picturesque American Midwestern city is turned into a dystopian nightmare. Men in balaclavas in unmarked cars drive down quiet snowy streets. At the Minneapolis airport, American vacationers gaze out the windows at shackled prisoners being dragged onboard planes nearby. A husband and wife hide in the trunk of a car as their son tries to sneak them past ICE officers.

They’re Here is Poitras’s first project since her Nan Goldin documentary All the Beauty and the Bloodshed, which won the festival’s Golden Lion in 2022 and later earned an Oscar nomination. Poitras previously won the best documentary Oscar in 2015 for Citizenfour, her landmark account of Edward Snowden and his NSA surveillance disclosures.

highlights.title: José Pizarro’s recipe for grilled sardines with blackberry escabeche
highlights.summary: A winning combination of oily fish, sweet berries and a sharp dressing. One of my favourite summer memories is making collares de moras as a child in Extremadura, which involved threading wild blackberries on to a piece of straw to make little necklaces.
body: Heat a tablespoon of the oil, then gently fry the shallots and bell pepper for six or seven minutes, until lovely and tender. Add the thyme and spices, fry for a minute more, then add the vinegar, wine and 100ml water, bring to a simmer and cook until the liquid has reduced by about half. Stir in the blackberries, then take off the heat and leave to cool slightly.

Meanwhile, put the rest of the oil in a large nonstick frying pan on a high heat. Season the butterflied sardines inside and out, then fry them skin-side down for three or four minutes, until golden and crisp. Flip over and fry for just a minute longer on the flesh side.

Arrange the cooked sardines skin-side up and side by side in a suitable deep-sided dish, pour the warm escabeche all over the top, then leave to marinate and cool down for at least an hour. Serve at once, or cover and chill in the fridge until you’re ready to eat.

highlights.title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims
highlights.summary: Users say they are losing money or risk having their accounts suspended because Meta struggles to identify scammers.
body: Instagram creators say they have lost thousands of pounds after their accounts were suspended or taken down due to fake copyright claims.
Extorters have filed bogus claims to the Meta-owned social media platform, then asked for ransoms to withdraw them - knowing repeated claims can lead to account bans.

One Instagram user, who has 1.5 million followers, told the BBC he paid a scammer $50 (£37) to get his account back, claiming Meta's appeal process would take weeks, which had previously cost him thousands in lost income.
"We understand this can be frustrating for those impacted, and our systems are designed to protect people from this happening in the first place," a Meta spokesperson said.

highlights.title: Whispering Complaints Into Your Phone May Be the Future of Customer Feedback
highlights.summary: Forget email surveys or long calls spent on hold. Voicebox lets people send customer feedback by recording a voice note on their phone.
body: Some of the hottest software this year revolves around capturing voices. Whether it’s the sharp dictations of Wispr or the always-listening ears of Granola, voice-centered software currently feels inescapable. Voice dictation is getting so sharp, in fact, that I often write drafts in my notepad and then dictate aloud to my laptop.

Some prognosticators have declared this to be a dramatic end-of-the-keyboard moment, where legions of white-collar workers will soon be quietly whispering into desk microphones rather than clacking away at keyboards. I disagree, but I do think these changes could upend how customers give feedback.

I rarely email customer support unless something substantially negative has happened and I’m fishing for a refund. I’m much more open to giving feedback by blabbering for 20 seconds into my phone, good or bad, than I am to waiting on hold for who knows how long until someone answers.

highlights.title: How Calafiori has become 'the best left-back in the league by far'
highlights.summary: Riccardo Calafiori returns to Italy with Arsenal this week - and he's a very different player compared to the one who departed for England two years ago.
body: When Arsenal came in for Calafiori, he was regularly playing at centre-back at Bologna. Those who guided his career had doubts about whether he could reach the highest level as a left-back.
But now, Calafiori is not just thriving as a left-back for the Premier League champions. "He's the best left-back in the league by far," says Jamie Carragher.

As well as being part of an imperious Arsenal defence, the Italian has started this season on fire in front of goal, scoring in the Community Shield win over Manchester City and getting assists in the league victories over Coventry and Aston Villa.
VAR spotting an offside Ezri Konsa denied Calafiori getting on the scoresheet against Chelsea, but the Italian did have a crucial role in Arsenal's winning goal, scored by Martin Odegaard.

highlights.title: How Grotesqqque Turns One Creator's Unfiltered Imagination Into an Anime Anthology
highlights.summary: Atsushi Nishigori has spent much of his career inside the machinery of others' anime. His years at Gainax — the hugely influential studio behind FLCL and Neon Genesis Evangelion — put him in the orbit of creators like Hiroyuki Imaishi and Kazuya Tsurumaki.
body: With Grotesqqque, CloverWorks’ new anthology film set to release in November, Nishigori finally has a chance to let his imagination run rampant. In a conversation with Polygon, Nishigori unpacked the three wildly different stories at the heart of Grotesqqque, his visual-first approach to animation, and the creative freedom that came with finally making something entirely his own. Ever-present in his mind were the characters and designs he had spent years waiting to bring to life.

“There were always a lot of scenes and character designs that I had wanted to do in the past, and I had just been piling them up inside me,” Nishigori told Polygon through a translator. “I really wanted to bring all of those ideas I had in my mind into this work, so I asked the company to let me make something where I could do whatever I wanted.”

highlights.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the cockroaches were everywhere – even on our wine glasses
highlights.summary: In a cheap London flat with no heating, dozens of the insects swarmed, leading to a Valentine’s Day that still makes me break out in a cold sweat. I don’t know if cockroaches really could, as we’re often told, survive a nuclear apocalypse, but I can tell you this with certainty: they can definitely…
body: It was January 2003 when I moved with my girlfriend Helen into our first London flat. It’s fair to say there were red flags we probably should have spotted. It was suspiciously affordable – £140 a week for a place less than a minute’s walk from Finsbury Park tube station? Sure, the place looked pretty skanky, but it was still spacious for a studio flat. We put the price down to the fact there was absolutely no way of heating the property and signed up.
That winter was bleak – we were freezing cold and, worse, waking up each morning with lines of red bites down our arms and legs. It took us a while to work out the culprits: bedbugs.

Bug spray was deployed, but it just made them angrier – the bites actually got worse. We replaced the mattress and that problem disappeared. (Despite not having encountered bedbugs anywhere since, Helen still checks down the the headboards in every hotel she stays at and won’t let her kids leave their bags on the floor.) The true horror, though, was yet to come.

highlights.title: First Xiaomi, then the world: why Arm might give phone gaming a huge graphics boost
highlights.summary: China is getting first crack at a British technology that might change how mobile games are made and played. Today, the Xiaomi 18 Fold launches in mainland China with an Arm Mali G2-Ultra NX graphics processor inside its custom Xring O3 chip. What's so special about that?
body: By following Nvidia’s playbook, Arm-powered phones are about to have PC-like technologies to make games run faster, at higher resolution, with advanced lighting techniques, all without using more power than they do today. The jagged edges you see in the mobile versions of popular games might begin to go away.
And these advancements won’t just be locked to Chinese phones. The chips, devices, and games are already inbound.

“You will be able to buy it; you will be able to get it in phones next year, you will be able to get it in other types of larger screen devices, whether that be tablets or Chromebooks,” Arm’s Chris Bergey, EVP of Edge AI, tells The Verge in an interview.
While he can’t say which other devices will contain the Mali G2-Ultra NX, he hints that some of Google’s upcoming Googlebooks might use this graphics tech as well.

highlights.title: Supporting independent journalism in Ukraine
highlights.summary: OpenAI, AIRPPU and WAN-IFRA launch an AI program to help Ukrainian news organizations strengthen innovation, resilience, and independent journalism.
body: Working with WAN-IFRA and AIRPPU to protect and rebuild independent journalism through conflict in Ukraine.
The following was issued as a joint press release on Monday 7th September 2026 from WAN-IFRA, AIRPPU, and OpenAI.
The Newsroom AI Masterclass Series and Newsroom AI Catalyst support Ukraine’s independent news sector with a focus on AI adoption, innovation, and resilience.

OpenAI, WAN-IFRA, and the Association of Independent Regional Press Publishers of Ukraine (AIRPPU) have announced a new initiative to support and strengthen Ukrainian news publishers by building practical artificial intelligence capabilities and accelerating innovation across their organisations. body: It’s been smooth sailing for the Rams, with their collection of playmakers growing by the day. It’s a very different story for the 49ers: facing Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, not to mention the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks, at least twice this season is the least of their problems. Their offseason has been more than lightly turbulent: it’s been batshit crazy.

The history of NFL scandals is Mariana Trench deep, and every season a unique calamity pops up. Meet Daejon Love, 49ers wide receiver, wealthy investor and a Casanova on the prowl. At least that’s what the 26 women Love allegedly defrauded out of $1.3m are said to have believed. Love, who it turns out is decidedly not a San Francisco 49er, was arrested last month by the FBI and has been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. It’s unclear what is more bonkers: Love’s apparent audacity or the fact that none of the women he is said to have defrauded appear to have googled their new “NFL player” boyfriend.

body: A decade into Instagram’s reign over fashion, keeping pace with the changing platform and the ways people use it has become something of a holy grail for fashion marketers. But lately, the conversation has become about much more than reach or engagement.

Virality has lost some of its luster; some people are retreating to smaller, niche platforms where there’s still room to be “messy” online; influencers are burning out, while brands are investing in real-world communities as consumers tire of life mediated through a screen. And yet, for all the talk of a social media backlash, we’re hardly logging off: in the UK, time spent on Instagram has risen by 60% in the last two years according to Ofcom, and Gen Z adults in the US spend an average of an hour a day on the platform, per Emarketer’s count.

highlights.title: Xiaomi 18 Fold hands-on: An attractive 'mid-size' foldable with powerful specs
highlights.summary: Xiaomi's impressive-sounding new foldable arrives on the eve of Apple's big foldable iPhone event.
body: The stockier foldable lands in China the same week Apple is expected to announce its own.

Xiaomi has formally launched what it's calling its first-ever "mid-size" foldable, the Xiaomi 18 Fold. It combines a 7.68-inch foldable display with a 5.38-inch outer display, both in a new, even more... squished aspect ratio. Xiaomi is trumpeting its A4 aspect ratio across both screens, creating a more unified feel when transitioning between them. At 219g, it's also the lightest foldable the company has ever made.

Interestingly, the front display has an asymmetric notepad look, with the right edge corners curved while the hinge-edge corners are square. This helps the device stand out even more when so many foldables seem to hit the same design notes. On the eve of Apple revealing its first foray into foldables, I got to spend a little time with Xiaomi's passport-style smartphone during IFA, and (just like the Galaxy Z Fold 8) I'm smitten with this stockier frame. And the stunning red color.

highlights.title: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement
highlights.summary: Authors say publishers seem to be claiming more than their fair share of settlement payments.
body: Some authors hoping to receive their share of Anthropic’s $1.5 billion copyright settlement said they received surprising emails this week — emails informing them that someone else was making a claim on their payments.

Anthropic settled a copyright class action suit last year, after a judge ruled that training AI models on copyrighted material is legal under fair use doctrine, but pirating that material was not. The deal received final approval in July, allowing the payments to move forward.

Under the terms of the settlement, the authors of nearly 500,000 titles will be paid $3,000 for each pirated work. If the book is still in print with a traditional publisher, the money will be split 50-50 between author and publisher. If the book was self-published, or if the publisher reverted the rights by allowing the book to go out of print, then the author should get the entire payment.
points: Authors say publishers seem to be claiming more than their fair share of settlement payments.

If you've been waiting for a restock, this is probably one worth considering while the stock lasts. These don't tend to hang around for long when they appear at major retailers.

highlights.title: A New Luxury Marketplace Is Making Adaptive Fashion More Discoverable
highlights.summary: Weldun founder and CEO Carly Berlin’s new marketplace is built on the premise that functional clothing exists in luxury already — and can be big business.
body: Before her preventative double mastectomy, artist and designer Carly Berlin’s favorite brand to shop was Kallmeyer. Post-double mastectomy, Kallmeyer remained a favorite, thanks to the adaptability of many of the brand’s garments.

“Just because something is functional doesn’t mean that it can’t be beautiful. You see that all the time in interior design, but it’s really not a part of the conversation in fashion,” Berlin says. Recovering from her surgery, she wondered why the tie between functionality and beauty remained so underexamined in fashion. She connected with other women going through surgeries, treatments, and moments of physical change — and nobody knew where to look for fashion in these moments.

In the wake of her mastectomy, Berlin lived in Skims and Negative Underwear — and then gifted those same pieces to friends going through their own transitionary moments. After sending so many of her contacts the pieces she had discovered during hours of searching, Berlin decided to create the discovery layer for pieces that are tasteful, beautiful, and, most importantly, wearable.
